text: Why is the telephone network's DS0 exactly 64 kb/s?
choices: It was chosen arbitrarily for administrative convenience
8,000 samples/s (Nyquist for a 3.4 kHz signal, with filter headroom) x 8 bits per sample
It is the maximum an analog local loop can carry
It matches the T1 rate divided by 24
explanation: Telephone speech is band-limited to about 3.4 kHz, so Nyquist requires at least 6.8 kHz sampling; 8 kHz was chosen to leave a transition band for realisable anti-aliasing filters. Eight bits per sample gives 8,000 x 8 = 64,000 b/s. The T1 rate is derived from the DS0, not the other way round.
